spec_coverage.notes: Every SPEC §12 item maps to a behavioral, falsifiable example — no gaps. #show covers all six §5.3 states (never-ran, first-extraction-running, succeeded, regenerating-over-success, zero-criteria-failure, other-failure). #create covers pending-row+enqueue-with(row_id, org_user.id), blank/flipper 422 with exact messages and no row, in_progress/retrying no-op, draft+published. GHOST-TEST SWEEP CLEAN: no reflection-only assertions (no instance_method/rescue_handlers/always-true type checks/unused vars); every test calls the real code path and asserts on side effects (change(count), have_been_enqueued.with, GlobalChannel.broadcast_to, have_enqueued_job, response status + parsed body, expect_any_instance_of(Job).not_to receive(:extract_job_criteria_if_needed) + Orchestrate.not_to receive(:new)). RULE 4 SATISFIED: bulk_generate_ai_summaries_job_spec zero-criteria batch stubs BulkJobApplicationAiSummaryResultMailer.failed => instance_double(ActionMailer::MessageDelivery, deliver_later: true) and asserts have_received(:deliver_later); it is the only mailer-delivery-relevant path in the diff (the extract job broadcasts over GlobalChannel, no mailer). AUTH DELTA FALSIFIABLE AND LOAD-BEARING: hiring-team context creates a real HiringTeamMembership(organization_user, job) and runs the real Pundit policy (no pundit_user override => default current_user; policy not stubbed). Member is role :org_user (not admin) with settings['hiring_team_ai_credits_control_enabled']=false. Under the NEW gate update? = on_hiring_team? = is_org_admin? || record.users.include?(user); record.users flows through hiring_team_memberships so the member is included => allowed (test expects :ok). Under the OLD gate update_ai_settings? = can_use_ai_credits? = is_org_admin? || (is_org_user? && hiring_team_ai_credits_control_enabled?) => false||(true&&false) => rejected. The explicit control=false setting is load-bearing (flip it to true and the old gate would also allow, killing falsifiability). Outsider context is role :org_user, no membership, not admin => update? false => 403; falsifiable (removing authorize would yield 200/422). Both share the same org so the exists() lookup finds the job and authorize (not a 404) is what rejects — the member's passing #show test in the same org confirms the lookup pipeline resolves. All referenced lets/helpers exist (create_credit_test_job defaults description 'Test job description'; create_credit_test_organization_user defaults :org_admin but auth contexts explicitly pass :org_user). No test coverage gaps, no ghost tests, no untraceable spec-file changes in my focus area.
